question: Why does the Lord say all beings stand in Him while He is not situated in them?
premises: The whole world is pervaded by me in unmanifest form.
I am not situated in them.
Even long considering that all beings stand in me, there is no other support-abode.
In the appearance of beings, concealment of opposite knowledge-nature occurs by making inert form preceded by known self-nature.
Therefore it is said: I am not situated in them.
inference: The Lord pervades and supports all beings without being contained or limited by them; their apparent inert form conceals the opposite knowledge-nature.
uncertainties: The long compound glosses are approximate and may not fully capture the commentary's technical sense.
plain_english: I pervade this whole world in unmanifest form; all beings stand in me, yet I am not situated in them. Even considering for long that all beings stand in me, there is no other support-abode; in their appearance, the opposite knowledge-nature is concealed by making inert form preceded by the known self-nature. Thus it is said: I am not situated in them.
